title: API 580 Training: Risk Based Inspection Exam Prep Online
description: API 580 exam prep: self-paced online study of API RP 580 risk based inspection, POF, COF, risk matrices and damage mechanisms, with instructor Q&A.
h1: API 580 Training and Exam Prep: Risk Based Inspection, Self-Paced Online
html:
API 580 is the certification for people who need to show they understand risk-based inspection: how an RBI program is planned, how probability and consequence of failure are assessed, how risk is ranked and managed, and how the work is recorded and kept current. Unlike the API 510, 570 and 653 examinations, it is one closed-book paper built on one document, API Recommended Practice 580. Below: what that paper covers, the RBI ideas it returns to, how to study for it, and how the self-paced course and its instructor Q&A fit around a full-time job.

The American Petroleum Institute (API) sets eligibility, administers the API 580 examination and issues the certification, and each candidate applies to API directly. Passing shows knowledge of RP 580. It does not by itself make anyone an RBI practitioner: running an assessment on a real unit takes data, a qualified team and the owner's approval of the results.

What the API 580 exam tests, and is it open book?

The API 580 examination has 90 multiple-choice questions, 80 scored and 10 unscored pretest questions, in 3.25 hours. It is closed-book: no reference material is allowed and nothing may be taken into the test room. API grades it against a set passing scaled score. API's programme page says the exam can be taken at an in-person test centre or by remote proctoring; confirm the options for your window when you apply.

The 2026 Body of Knowledge bases the exam on API RP 580, Elements of a Risk-Based Inspection Program, 4th Edition (August 2023) with Addendum 1 (March 2025), and focuses on the most recent edition. It lists ten knowledge categories and nothing beneath them, and it has no calculation section of the kind the inspector certifications carry. API 580 therefore tests understanding and precise vocabulary more than arithmetic, so candidates who are strong on the inspection codes should not expect the paper to play to that strength: it asks why an RBI program does what it does.

Who takes API 580, and how eligibility works

API describes API 580 as a certification for inspectors, engineers and other petrochemical professionals with a thorough knowledge of RBI. In practice candidates include API 510, 570 and 653 inspectors whose sites have moved to risk-based intervals, corrosion and materials engineers who sit on RBI teams, mechanical integrity and reliability engineers, inspection planners who maintain RBI models, and managers who approve risk-based inspection plans.

  • Holders of a current API 510, API 570 or API 653 certification qualify automatically.
  • Everyone else qualifies through education plus petrochemical industry experience gained in the last ten years: one year with a bachelor's degree or higher in engineering or technology, two years with a two-year degree or certificate, three years with a high school diploma or equivalent, and five or more years with no formal education.

Experience is documented on the application and API decides whether it qualifies; the course does not count as experience. Because the experience required is petrochemical industry experience rather than work for an authorized inspection agency, API 580 is open to engineers and analysts who will never sit the inspector papers. If you are weighing the inspector certifications as well, see which API certification to take first.

The ten knowledge areas in the API 580 Body of Knowledge

Because the Body of Knowledge gives headings only, the detail has to come from RP 580 itself. The table pairs each category with what a candidate should be able to explain without the text.

API 580 Body of Knowledge categories
Knowledge areaWhat you should be able to explain
Terms, definitions and acronymsRP 580's own meaning of risk, probability of failure (POF), consequence of failure (COF), damage mechanism, loss of containment and the acronyms the document uses
Risk assessmentRisk as the combination of probability and consequence; qualitative, semi-quantitative and quantitative approaches and what each needs and delivers
RBI programPlanning: objectives, scope (units, systems, equipment), choice of method and how RBI fits the existing inspection program
Roles, responsibilities, training and qualificationsWho sits on the RBI team, what each member contributes and the competence expected of those who perform and approve assessments
Data collectionDesign, construction, process, inspection and maintenance data; how data quality and missing records affect results
Damage mechanismsScreening credible mechanisms for each item and telling rate-driven thinning from susceptibility-driven cracking
POFHow mechanism, rate or susceptibility, time in service and inspection effectiveness combine into a probability of failure
COFFlammable, toxic, environmental and business consequences and what drives each
Risk managementUsing the ranking: inspection planning, mitigation other than inspection, and keeping the assessment current
RBI documentationWhat must be recorded so an assessment can be audited, repeated and updated

Core RBI concepts the API 580 exam keeps returning to

Risk is probability and consequence together

RBI ranks equipment by risk, the combination of the probability that an item loses containment and the consequence if it does. Two items can share a risk category for opposite reasons: a lightly damaged line in a highly toxic service is consequence-driven, while a badly corroded line in a mild service is probability-driven. You need to be able to tell which side drives the risk, because the right action depends on it. Inspection works mainly on the probability side, by reducing uncertainty about the damage state; it does little to the consequence of a release.

Qualitative, semi-quantitative and quantitative

RP 580 does not endorse one methodology. It sets minimum expectations for a quality assessment and describes a continuum from qualitative analysis, built on categories and judgment, through semi-quantitative, to quantitative analysis with numerical probability and consequence from detailed models. Know the trade-offs: the data each approach needs, the effort, repeatability, and how finely the results separate one item from the next.

Risk matrices

Results are often shown on a risk matrix with probability categories on one axis and consequence categories on the other; a five-by-five grid with numbered probability and lettered consequence categories is a common layout, with the cells banded from low to high risk. Be ready to read a matrix: which items move when inspection is credited (they move along the probability axis), which do not, and why an item in a high-consequence column can stay high however often it is inspected.

Probability of failure and inspection effectiveness

POF starts from the damage mechanisms an item is exposed to, their likely rate or severity, and time in service. Inspection effectiveness then describes how well past and planned inspections would detect and size that damage: the right method for the mechanism, in the right places, with enough coverage. A spot thickness survey is effective against general thinning and close to useless against stress corrosion cracking, so crediting it against cracking overstates confidence. RP 581 grades effectiveness from A (highly effective) to E (ineffective), a scale worth recognising even though the exam is set on RP 580.

Consequence of failure

COF estimates what a loss of containment would cause: fire and explosion, toxic exposure, environmental damage and business interruption. The drivers are the fluid and its phase, the inventory that could be released, the release rate and how quickly a leak is detected and isolated. Practice questions change one of these, such as adding isolation valves, and ask what happens to the risk ranking.

What RBI cannot compensate for

An RBI assessment cannot make up for inaccurate data, inadequate design or installation, operation outside acceptable limits, or failure to act on the findings. RP 580 also positions RBI alongside other programmes rather than in place of them: it is not a substitute for a process hazards analysis or HAZOP, and it complements reliability-centred maintenance. These boundaries are easy marks once read.

Damage mechanisms, API RP 571 and the 580 exam

Damage mechanisms are one of the ten categories, and an assessment is only as good as its damage mechanism review. RP 580 points to API RP 571 for descriptions of the mechanisms found in refining and petrochemical equipment. For the exam you need the logic more than the metallurgy: how a mechanism is screened in or out from material, temperature, process stream and history; the difference between a thinning mechanism with a rate and a cracking mechanism with a susceptibility; and why a feed change, a new injection point or a temperature excursion should send the team back to the review. The course uses familiar RP 571 examples such as CUI, chloride stress corrosion cracking, sour water and amine service to make the ideas concrete. For working detail see API 571 damage mechanisms and how a damage mechanism review is run.

The RBI team, data and documentation

RBI is team work, and roles are one of the ten categories. A typical team has a team leader, an equipment inspector or inspection specialist, a materials and corrosion specialist, a process specialist, operations and maintenance people and someone skilled in risk analysis, with management responsible for resources and for acting on the results. Know who supplies what: the corrosion specialist the mechanisms and rates, the process specialist the stream conditions, the inspector the history and the effectiveness of past inspections.

On data, quality matters more than lists: what an assumption does to the result when a record is missing, and why conservative defaults push items up the ranking. Documentation closes the loop, because an assessment that cannot show its inputs, assumptions, method and results cannot be audited, repeated or updated. RP 580 makes reassessing and updating the assessment an element of the program; many sites call this evergreening. Reassessment follows events such as new inspection results, a feed or operating change, an unexpected failure or a revamp, and also time; where an assessment sets inspection intervals, the governing inspection code (API 510, 570 or 653) adds its own rules on who reviews and approves it and how often.

RP 580 and RP 581: what the exam covers

Candidates often ask whether they need API RP 581. RP 580 sets out the elements every RBI program should have whatever method it uses; RP 581 is API's quantitative RBI methodology, with the models behind probability and consequence. The 2026 Body of Knowledge names RP 580 as the publication examined, and RP 581 is not on it. Learn RP 581 when your job needs it. Its vocabulary (damage factors, inspection effectiveness categories, risk targets) helps you read RP 580, but exam answers come from RP 580's text. Background: API 581 quantitative RBI and quantitative RBI in practice.

An API 580 study plan, phase by phase

Because the course is self-paced, the plan is set by what you can do, not by a calendar. Move on when you pass the check without notes.

  1. Read RP 580 straight through in the edition your window's Body of Knowledge names. Check: you can list the elements of an RBI program.
  2. Build the vocabulary. Make your own glossary from the definitions section. Check: you can define POF, COF, risk and inspection effectiveness in RP 580's words.
  3. Work the logic. Risk assessment, POF, COF and risk management with practice matrices: credit an inspection, change a consequence driver and see what moves. Check: you can explain a matrix to someone new to RBI.
  4. Program and people. Planning, team roles, data, documentation and reassessment. Check: you can say who supplies each input and what must be recorded.
  5. Closed-book practice. Timed 90-question papers, reviewed question by question against the clause that answers each one. Check: steady scores with time to spare.

Questions to the instructor tend to be about wording: why two definitions differ, whether a scenario is consequence- or probability-driven, or why an inspection earns less credit than expected. Answers point back to the RP 580 text.

Closed-book technique for API 580

  • Pace: 195 minutes for 90 questions is a little over two minutes each; most need less, so bank time for the ones you have to read twice.
  • Answer from RP 580, not your site's RBI manual, which may use different terms or thresholds.
  • Be wary of absolutes. Options claiming RBI eliminates risk or always reduces inspection misread a document that describes managing risk.
  • Split every scenario into probability and consequence before you read the options.
  • The ten pretest questions are unmarked and indistinguishable, so give every question the same care.

API 580 exam prep and RBI services

Atlantis also performs remote RBI studies for owner-operators, covering damage mechanism review, probability and consequence assessment, risk ranking and inspection plans, with the owner's inspector of record approving the resulting intervals; see risk-based inspection services. That work and this course are separate. The course prepares you for API's examination; it is not RBI practitioner training, it is not part of an RBI engagement, and the certificate is not authority to approve an assessment. Fitness-for-service assessment to API 579-1/ASME FFS-1 is a different discipline and is not part of the API 580 exam or this course.

Sponsoring API 580 candidates

Sites introducing or revalidating RBI often want the inspection lead, the corrosion engineer and the planners all able to challenge the results. Employers can sponsor several candidates; each studies at their own pace with access to the instructor and applies to API individually. Fees are quoted on request. Inspectors who already hold API 510, 570 or 653 bring the equipment knowledge, and what they add here is RP 580's framework and vocabulary.

faq.q: Is the API 580 exam open book?
faq.a: No. API 580 is closed-book: 90 multiple-choice questions in 3.25 hours with no reference material. That is the main difference from the API 510, 570 and 653 exams, which have an open-book part with code PDFs on screen. You need RP 580’s definitions and logic in your head.

faq.q: Do I need API 510, 570 or 653 before API 580?
faq.a: No. A current API 510, 570 or 653 certification qualifies you automatically, but it is not required. Without one, you qualify on education plus petrochemical industry experience from the last ten years, from one year with an engineering or technology degree to five or more years with no formal education.

faq.q: Is API RP 581 on the API 580 exam?
faq.a: Not under the 2026 Body of Knowledge, which names API RP 580, 4th Edition with Addendum 1, as the publication examined. RP 581 is the quantitative method and worth knowing for work, but exam answers come from RP 580. Check the Body of Knowledge for your own window in case that changes.

faq.q: Are there calculations on the API 580 exam?
faq.a: The Body of Knowledge has no calculation section, unlike the inspector exams. Expect to reason with probability and consequence categories, read risk matrices and judge inspection effectiveness rather than work long formulas. Knowing how risk moves when probability or consequence changes is the core skill.

The exam-prep course is self-paced online. The examination is API’s: its programme page says API 580 can be taken at an in-person test centre or by remote proctoring. Confirm the delivery options for your window when you schedule with API, since they are API’s to set and can change.

faq.q: Does passing API 580 make me an RBI analyst?
faq.a: No. It shows you know RP 580. Running an assessment needs the unit’s data, a suitable methodology, a qualified team, and the owner’s review and approval of the results. Treat the certification as the foundation for taking part in RBI work, not as the work itself.

faq.q: Which edition of RP 580 should I study?
faq.a: The edition named in the Body of Knowledge for your exam window. The 2026 Body of Knowledge names the 4th Edition (August 2023) with Addendum 1 (March 2025). If API issues a new Body of Knowledge before your window, that document governs what you study.

faq.q: How do I keep API 580 certification?
faq.a: API 580 certification lasts three years. You can apply to recertify through the ICP Portal from 90 days before expiry, with a 90-day grace period that carries late fees, and API does not currently require employment verification. If the grace period passes, you need a new application and the full exam.
